principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization
Follow consistency of logic across Lattice lifecycle gates
drivers: A code-changing story should not reach DONE with zero review evidence
Small tasks can still introduce bugs after low-risk PLAN classification
Full 3x2 on every code change would over-spend token/time budget
Local Non-authority review evidence must remain separate from Authority Server receipts

options.name: A: Minimum review floor plus failure-triggered 3x1 escalation
pros: Blocks zero-review code DONE while keeping low-risk work lightweight
Escalates after real bug, validation fail, reviewer finding, or rework signals
Fits existing degraded-single-host vocabulary without claiming two-host independence
cons: Requires a future implementation story to add mechanical DONE-oracle consumption and exact storage fields

options.name: B: Force every code change through three local single-host rounds
pros: Maximizes consistency and is easy to explain
Would have caught more small-task regressions before DONE
cons: Over-applies heavy review to clean trivial code changes and increases token/time cost without a real failure signal

options.name: C: Keep current threshold-triggered review escalation only
pros: No new policy surface and no implementation work beyond current gates
Avoids changing current DONE closure behavior
cons: Does not solve the observed correctness gap: a low-risk code task can still reach DONE with no minimum review floor

chosen: A: Minimum review floor plus failure-triggered 3x1 escalation
rationale: Choose A because the real correctness issue is not that every code task lacks full 3x2 review; it is that code-changing stories can have no review floor, and stories with actual failure signals need stronger closure. A preserves token discipline while making the missing minimum mechanical in a future implementation.

preMortem.scenario: The future implementation treats 3x1 as equivalent to two-host review
preMortem.trigger: Status output or summary says two-host passed when only one host submitted verdicts
preMortem.consequence: Lattice overclaims assurance and confuses local Non-authority evidence with independent host proof
preMortem.mitigation: Require assuranceLevel=degraded-single-host for 3x1 and forbid authorityDone/fullAuthorityDone/productionDone from local host verdicts

preMortem.scenario: The policy over-escalates every tiny code change to three rounds
preMortem.trigger: DONE oracle requires 3x1 merely because any source file changed
preMortem.consequence: Token usage rises sharply and developers bypass Lattice for small fixes
preMortem.mitigation: Keep clean ordinary code at one review round; escalate to 3x1 only after bug, validation fail, finding, rework, or explicit risk class

preMortem.scenario: The policy misses a bug because failure signals are not sticky
preMortem.trigger: A validation fail or bug is fixed, then evidence is removed or ignored before DONE
preMortem.consequence: The story returns to ordinary closure despite having shown real instability
preMortem.mitigation: Make failure-triggered review escalation sticky for the story material until DONE or explicit human degraded fallback
